assumptions: Preventable quote or handover errors occur often enough in the target installer segment to create annual savings above subscription cost.
Permissioned historical or synthetic cases adequately support initial validation without customer-data rights.
Human approval can contain liability without eliminating the product's labor savings.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A blinded test on at least 50 permissioned quotes showing material errors caught, measured avoided losses, acceptable false positives, and several independent installers paying and renewing at the proposed price.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Embedding maintained equipment and OSD checks at quote approval and handover directly targets preventable margin leakage and delayed invoices.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Margin errors and rejected paperwork can be costly, but their frequency and installer willingness to pay 900-1,800 PLN monthly are untested.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid setup plus recurring SaaS offers good cash conversion and plausible high margins, although support, rule maintenance, churn, CAC, and owner earnings remain modeled.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish renewable installers with 5-50 staff form a coherent, reachable niche with repeat workflows, though very small firms may remain spreadsheet users.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A Polish equipment-and-OSD rules layer can win a focused workflow, but CRM vendors and wholesalers can add similar validation.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: The product can extend into batteries, heat pumps, procurement, estimator training, compliance packs, and margin benchmarking.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: An anonymized error taxonomy and continuously maintained rules library can compound, but inputs are obtainable and access is nonexclusive.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Preventing one material quote error could repay the product quickly, giving a clear value proposition if detection accuracy is demonstrated.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Equipment variety and administrative handover complexity support adoption, but the micro-installation process can be relatively streamlined.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The family installer is a practical design route and wholesalers or associations could aggregate demand, although no channel or subscription is committed.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The low-capital, AI-assisted product fits part-time technical execution; principal risks are rule upkeep, workflow integration, and liability from incorrect checks.

highest_value_structural_change: Turn the rules engine into a wholesaler-embedded quote gate with contracted distribution and continuously supplied product-data updates.
main_structural_strength: A narrow recurring workflow connects an avoidable financial loss to a low-capital subscription product that suits the founder's access and skills.
primary_score_limiter: Neither the actual loss frequency nor willingness to adopt and pay for a new approval gate has been demonstrated beyond the family access path.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Small installers may tolerate spreadsheets, and streamlined micro-installation paperwork could make the proposed subscription cost exceed the recurring pain.
